title: Area and Perimeter Formulas
description: Learn area and perimeter formulas for rectangles and squares in Class 4 Maths. Find missing sides, calculate fencing costs, solve word problems. 10 MCQs and 6 IMO questions for exam preparation.

topics.title: Perimeter of Rectangle and Square
topics.concept:
Perimeter is the total distance around the outside of a shape — like walking around the boundary of a park.

Rectangle:
Perimeter = 2 x (Length + Width)
P = 2 x (l + w)

Why? A rectangle has 2 equal lengths and 2 equal widths.

Square:
All four sides are equal.
Perimeter = 4 x side (P = 4s)

To find a missing side: rearrange the formula. E.g. if P = 36 and l = 10, then 36 = 2(10+w), so w = 8.

topics.title: Area of Rectangle and Square
topics.concept:
Area is the amount of space INSIDE a shape. Think of it as the number of 1x1 squares that can fit inside.

Rectangle:
Area = Length x Width (A = l x w)

Square:
Area = side x side (A = s x s = s²)

Units: perimeter uses cm/m, but area uses square units — cm² or m².

To find a missing side when area is given: divide. E.g. if A = 54, l = 9, then w = 54 / 9 = 6.

examples.problem: A rectangular hall is 15 m long and 10 m wide. Find its area.
examples.solution: A = l x w = 15 x 10 = 150 m². Answer: 150 square metres.

examples.problem: A square tile has a side of 30 cm. What is its area?
examples.solution: A = s x s = 30 x 30 = 900 cm². Answer: 900 square centimetres.

examples.problem: A rectangle has an area of 54 cm². Its length is 9 cm. Find its width.
examples.solution: A = l x w. 54 = 9 x w. w = 54 / 9 = 6 cm. Answer: width = 6 cm.

recap: Area measures the space INSIDE a shape
Rectangle: A = l x w (length times width)
Square: A = s x s (side squared)
Area is always measured in square units: cm² or m²

topics.title: Relationship Between Area and Perimeter
topics.concept:
Area and perimeter are related but measure different things:

  • Perimeter = distance around (units: cm, m)
  • Area = space inside (square units: cm², m²)

Two shapes can have the same perimeter but different areas, or the same area but different perimeters!

This is an important insight: a square always has the largest area for a given perimeter compared to other rectangles.

examples.problem: A square has a perimeter of 48 cm. Find its area.
examples.solution: Step 1: Find side from perimeter. P = 4s. 48 = 4s. s = 12 cm. Step 2: Find area. A = s x s = 12 x 12 = 144 cm².

examples.problem: A square has an area of 64 m². Find its perimeter.
examples.solution: Step 1: Find side from area. A = s x s. 64 = s x s. s = 8 m (since 8 x 8 = 64). Step 2: Find perimeter. P = 4 x 8 = 32 m.

examples.problem: A farmer has a rectangular field 10 m x 25 m. Fencing costs Rs.15 per metre. Find the fencing cost and area of the field.
examples.solution: Perimeter = 2(10+25) = 2 x 35 = 70 m. Fencing cost = 70 x 15 = Rs.1,050. Area = 10 x 25 = 250 m².

recap: Same perimeter does NOT mean same area!
Square gives the largest area for a given perimeter
Perimeter units: cm, m (linear); Area units: cm2, m2 (square)
To find perimeter from area: first find the side, then use the formula
